events.title: Women's March on Versailles
events.description: Thousands of Parisian women, angered by bread shortages and high prices, marched to the Palace of Versailles and compelled King Louis XVI and the royal family to return to Paris.
events.significance: The march marked a turning point in the French Revolution, weakening royal authority and placing the monarchy under the direct influence of the Parisian populace.

events.title: Calcutta Cyclone
events.description: A devastating cyclone struck Calcutta and the surrounding Bengal region in British India, bringing a massive storm surge and destroying much of the shipping and many buildings in the area.
events.significance: One of the deadliest cyclones in recorded history, it killed an estimated 60,000 people and led to improved weather observation and warning efforts in India.

events.title: Release of Dr. No and 'Love Me Do'
events.description: On the same day, the first James Bond film, Dr. No, premiered in London, and The Beatles released their debut single, 'Love Me Do', in the United Kingdom.
events.significance: Both events launched enormously influential cultural phenomena: the long-running Bond film franchise and the global rise of The Beatles, which shaped popular music and film for decades.

events.title: Proclamation of the Portuguese Republic
events.description: Following a republican revolution in Lisbon, the monarchy of King Manuel II was overthrown and Portugal was declared a republic.
events.significance: The event ended more than 700 years of monarchy in Portugal and began the unstable First Portuguese Republic, which lasted until 1926.

events.title: Death of Steve Jobs
events.description: Steve Jobs, co-founder and former CEO of Apple Inc., died at age 56 after a long battle with pancreatic cancer.
events.significance: Jobs' death marked the loss of a pioneering technology innovator whose products, including the Macintosh, iPod, iPhone, and iPad, transformed personal computing, music, and mobile communication.
